title: A copy can be given its own color
goal: A component can offer a color as a knob, so one button original can produce a blue copy and a red copy without either of them leaving the family.
notes: Objective gap, not a rough line. Sources/PhotonzCore/ComponentProperties.swift:28 holds exactly three knob kinds today (text, visible, variant) and ComponentPropertyValue matches; docs/design/ui-building.md line 552 lists this as a deliberate first-version limit, and the epic promises create once, reuse everywhere, override safely. Reuse ColorStyles.swift and ColorStyleSelection.swift for the value and the mixed reading rather than writing a second one. Panel rows: Sources/Photonz/ComponentPanel.swift.
acceptance: A fill or an outline inside an original can be exposed as a knob, next to wording, show or hide, and choice
A copy shows that knob as a color row and answers it with the app own picker, the same picker every other color row opens
A copy that has not answered follows the original, and editing the original repaints every copy that has not
A saved named color can be the answer, so renaming or editing that color moves every copy that points at it
Over several copies the row reads Mixed the way every other control does, and setting it sets them all
Old documents decode unchanged, and a knob whose layer is gone is dropped rather than crashing

Ships behind next-components. To see it: open Photonz Next, draw a rectangle, make it a component, expose its fill, drop two copies from the Library, give one a different color, then edit the original fill and watch the untouched copy follow
Tests in PhotonzCore cover exposing, answering, clearing, the named-color case and the mixed reading before the app code is written
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task
